items.headline: Man who stabbed a priest during mass at St Joseph's Church jailed and caned
items.summary: Basnayake Keith Spencer, 38, was sentenced on Aug 21 to 4 years and 3 months' jail and 9 strokes of the cane for stabbing Father Christopher Lee during a children's mass in November 2024.

items.headline: JB-Singapore RTS Link enters final testing ahead of a January 2027 launch
items.summary: Media took a test ride on the cross-border RTS Link on Aug 17; Malaysia's transport minister Anthony Loke reaffirmed a Jan 1, 2027 passenger start and 10,000 commuters per hour each way.

items.headline: PM Wong to deliver the National Day Rally on Aug 23, with family support in focus
items.summary: PM Lawrence Wong delivers National Day Rally 2026 from ITE Headquarters in Ang Mo Kio on Aug 23, expected to outline measures helping families raise children and care for ageing parents.

items.headline: Sajjan Kumar, ex-Congress MP convicted in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, dies at 80
items.summary: Former three-time Outer Delhi MP Sajjan Kumar, serving concurrent life sentences over the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre, died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Aug 20 after being brought from Tihar Jail.

items.headline: Reliance proposes a Rs 2.73 lakh crore underground coal gasification complex in Andhra
items.summary: Reliance Industries filed a proposal to invest about Rs 2.73 lakh crore over 30 years to build India's first integrated underground coal gasification complex in Eluru district, Andhra Pradesh.

items.headline: Amit Shah chairs the Southern Zonal Council as water disputes and delimitation dominate
items.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah chaired the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting on Aug 20 near Mahabalipuram, where southern CMs raised Cauvery and Krishna river-sharing, Mekedatu, Mullaperiyar and delimitation.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds hanging as a constitutional method of execution
items.summary: A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta dismissed a plea to replace death by hanging with lethal injection, holding there was no reason to reconsider the 1983 Deena judgment.

items.headline: Supreme Court halts a disproportionate-assets case against Rahul Gandhi
items.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Allahabad High Court not to proceed with a disproportionate-assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi and told the CBI and ED not to file reports for now.

items.headline: UK July public borrowing hits £1.8bn, defying forecasts of a small surplus
items.summary: The ONS said public sector net borrowing was £1.8bn in July 2026, well above the roughly £500m surplus the OBR had forecast, sharpening the fiscal squeeze on Chancellor John Healey.

items.headline: UK retail sales fell 0.5% in July as clothing demand slumped
items.summary: ONS figures showed retail sales volumes dropped 0.5% in July 2026, with clothing down 2.7%, while GfK consumer confidence rose to a two-year high of minus 14 in August.

items.headline: Retail and hospitality bosses warn guaranteed-hours rules threaten jobs
items.summary: Chief executives of the British Retail Consortium, Food and Drink Federation and UKHospitality warned that guaranteed-hours reforms under the Employment Rights Act pose a substantial threat to jobs.

items.headline: Home Office records 230 migrants crossing the Channel on a single small boat
items.summary: The Home Office said 230 people crossed the English Channel on one small boat, the largest number ever recorded on a single vessel, even as 2026 crossings ran below 2025 levels.

items.headline: UAE suspends all trade and finance with Iran after an alleged missile attack
items.summary: The UAE indefinitely halted all trade and financial transactions with Iran after reporting two ballistic missiles fired from Iranian territory on Aug 18, a claim Tehran denied.

items.headline: US redesignates Hezbollah as an Iranian proxy and sanctions a cash-courier network
items.summary: The US Treasury re-designated Hezbollah a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under the IRGC-Quds Force and sanctioned 10 people in a courier network moving cash across Lebanon, Turkey, the UAE and Iran.

items.headline: Israeli strike kills at least six in Gaza City as the ceasefire stays stalled
items.summary: An Israeli strike hit a crowded seafront cafe in Gaza City, killing at least six and wounding 14 per al-Shifa Hospital, as the second phase of the ceasefire remained deadlocked.

items.headline: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life for fraud and bribery
items.summary: A Shenzhen court sentenced Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison for fraud and bribery and ordered his assets forfeited, after the developer collapsed with over $300bn in liabilities.

items.headline: Nevada approves up to 8,000 robotaxis for Tesla, Uber and Waymo
items.summary: The Nevada Transportation Authority approved permits letting Tesla deploy up to 5,000 robotaxis and Uber and Waymo up to 1,000 each in Clark County over the next year.

items.headline: Nvidia to pay Poolside about $6bn to license its AI model-building software
items.summary: Nvidia agreed to pay AI startup Poolside roughly $6bn to license its Model Factory software and hire about 109 staff, plus a $1bn investment at a $12bn valuation.

items.headline: Broadcom seeks more than $60bn in debt for an AI chip financing deal
items.summary: Broadcom is in talks with lenders to raise more than $60bn, potentially up to about $100bn, to finance an AI chip deal benefiting Anthropic and others.

items.headline: Starcloud raises $250m to build AI data centres that run in orbit
items.summary: Starcloud, developing satellites that perform AI inference in space, added a $250m extension to its Series A, valuing the company at about $2.3bn.

items.headline: Alibaba-backed robotics firm Dexmal seeks a $3bn valuation
items.summary: Chinese robotics startup Dexmal is seeking a valuation of around 20 billion yuan, about $3bn, underlining investor appetite for firms chasing physical AI.

items.headline: Wall Street rallies on Friday but posts a weekly loss as bonds weigh
items.summary: The Dow rose 517.80 points, or 0.98%, to 53,277.01 on Friday, with the S&P 500 up 0.43% to 7,674.37, but all three major indexes logged weekly losses amid a Treasury sell-off.

items.headline: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5.33%, its highest since 2007, as a bond rout deepens
items.summary: The 30-year US Treasury yield climbed to about 5.33% this week, its highest since 2007, amid a large deficit, heavy AI issuance and uncertainty under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

items.headline: Bitcoin climbs past $77,000 amid crypto-policy optimism
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $77,000 this week, its strongest run in over a year, helped by expanded Treasury bond buybacks and a White House push for the CLARITY Act; ether reached about $2,363.

items.headline: Walmart suffers its worst day in four years as US comparable sales slow
items.summary: Walmart shares fell about 9% on Aug 20, their worst session in over four years, after US comparable sales rose just 2.6% despite revenue up 5.9% to $187.9bn.

items.headline: Target beats estimates on 5.3% sales growth, aided by a $994m tariff refund
items.summary: Target reported second-quarter net sales of $26.5bn, up 5.3%, with comparable sales of 3.8% beating consensus and helped by $994m in tariff refunds; new CEO Michael Fiddelke touted growth.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell snatches Dutch GP sprint pole as Verstappen labours to sixth at home
items.summary: George Russell took his third sprint pole of 2026 at Zandvoort, pipping Lando Norris by 0.041s, with Verstappen only sixth on his final home Dutch Grand Prix.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli's title lead wobbles as leader and Hamilton falter in Zandvoort sprint qualifying
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli slid into the gravel and could only qualify fifth for the sprint, with nearest rival Lewis Hamilton seventh, leaving both title contenders on the back foot.

items.headline: 🎾 Sinner withdraws from the US Open with a knee injury as Zverev inherits the top seed
items.summary: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner pulled out of the US Open with a persistent right-knee problem; French Open champion Alexander Zverev becomes the top seed as the main draw begins Aug 30.

items.headline: 🎾 Sabalenka headlines the US Open entry list, chasing a third straight New York title
items.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka tops the 2026 US Open entry list as No. 1 seed, bidding to become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three straight US Opens.

items.headline: 🏏 India crush Sri Lanka by 165 runs in Galle as Suthar takes a 10-wicket haul
items.summary: India completed a 165-run win in the first Test at Galle, with Manav Suthar claiming ten match wickets and Devdutt Padikkal making 167; India lead the two-Test series 1-0.

items.headline: 🏏 England thrash Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley
items.summary: England beat Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs in the first Test at Leeds, bowling the tourists out for 135 in reply to 409; Harry Brook top-scored with 91.

items.headline: Astronomers identify a 'black hole star', a new class of cosmic object
items.summary: A team reported MoM-BH*-1, a young black hole cloaked in a dense hydrogen envelope that mimics a giant star's spectrum, possibly explaining JWST's 'little red dots'.

items.headline: Physicists build the first cyclic superconducting quantum heat engine near absolute zero
items.summary: Aalto University researchers built a nanoscale Otto-cycle heat engine using a transmon qubit and quantum-circuit refrigerator, the first cyclic quantum heat engine of its kind.

fun_fact.headline: The shortest war in history lasted about 38 minutes
fun_fact.body: The shortest war in recorded history was the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 27 August 1896, fought between Britain and the Sultanate of Zanzibar. It was over in roughly 38 minutes, and is still listed by Guinness World Records as the shortest war ever waged.

puzzle.title: The Long Push
puzzle.body: A man is pushing his car. When he arrives in front of a hotel, he immediately knows that he is bankrupt. He is not surprised, and no money changes hands. What is going on?
puzzle.approach: Question your assumptions about what kind of 'car' and 'hotel' these really are.
puzzle.answer: He is playing Monopoly. The 'car' is his playing token, which he moves around the board. He has landed on a property owned by another player that has a hotel on it, and the rent exceeds his remaining cash and assets, so he is out of the game.

word_puzzle.title: Table Talk
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter T; outer letters A B E L N O. Make words of 4+ letters that each include T; one pangram uses all seven letters.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must use the centre letter T; find the seven-letter word that uses all of them.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: NOTABLE. Other words include ATONE, BATON, BALLOT, BLEAT, BLOAT, BELT, BENT, BOAT, BOLT, BOTTLE, ELATE, LATTE, NOTE, OBLATE, TABLE, TALON, TEAL, TONAL, TONE, TOTAL.

Singapore ran 3 items and Other Miscellaneous News ran 2 items — below the floor of 4 — because allowed-source URL capture was blocked and the search budget was exhausted before more in-window items could be confirmed (fewer stories today, not padding).

Dropped for lack of a verifiable allowed source: a reported magnitude-7.4 Colombia earthquake (no allowed deep URL confirmable), and several frontier-science items that appeared only on off-list outlets.
